output.title: Why reviewer training is a bounded control
output.body:
Reviewer training helps, but it is not the whole control. If the same approval rules appear over and over, the weak point is often not knowledge. It is repeatable logic, data entry, fatigue, or an edge case that training alone will not remove. So the practical limit is simple: training can improve judgment, but it does not change the workflow itself.

The diagnostic question is: are most errors happening because the reviewer does not know the rule, or because the work still depends on the same manual check every time? If it is the second case, you are looking at a workflow problem, not a classroom problem.

A plain example: if an invoice or approval check always follows the same sequence, a tired person can still miss one step. A repeatable rule check can catch that kind of miss; a slide deck cannot. That is not a criticism of people. It is just how late afternoons work.

At Bareni, we focus on repeatable logic steps in small-business workflows, with human approval kept in place for exceptions and high-risk decisions. That is a policy choice, not a warranty.

A useful next step is to identify one recurring decision step that follows the same logic each time and note how often it appears. If it is truly repeatable, that is the point to examine before spending more time on training materials.
